data.title: Methoxsalen topical solution (topical PUVA)
data.summary: VIII Pigmentary / depigmenting · Psoralen (8-methoxypsoralen) for topical photochemotherapy
data.body:
_Topicals · VIII Pigmentary / depigmenting_

**Class:** Psoralen (8-methoxypsoralen) for topical photochemotherapy

## Mechanism of action
- Applied psoralen is activated by UVA/sunlight → DNA cross-linking, T-cell apoptosis
- In vitiligo: stimulates melanocyte proliferation, migration from hair follicle reservoirs, and melanogenesis

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Localised vitiligo (under 20% BSA), including children over about 5 years (oral PUVA not suitable)
- Localised palmoplantar psoriasis and hand/foot eczema (soak or paint PUVA)
- Alopecia areata (limited)

## Dose & formulations
- Commercial 1% lotion must be diluted (usually to 0.1% or lower, e.g. 1:10 with alcohol/acetone; Wolverton uses even lower 0.001–0.005% for bath/soak)
- Apply to patches only, 15–30 min before exposure to UVA or morning sunlight
- Start with 1–2 min of sun/low UVA, increase gradually; 2–3 times a week, never on consecutive days
- Wash the area after exposure and protect from further sun for the day

## Adverse effects
- Phototoxic reaction: severe erythema, blistering (common if undiluted or overexposed)
- Hyperpigmentation of surrounding skin (perilesional 'halo' or patchy darkening)
- Contact dermatitis
- Less systemic risk than oral PUVA (no nausea, eye protection less critical, but avoid getting it near eyes)

## Contraindications
- Photosensitive disorders (lupus, porphyria, XP), children under 5
- Pregnancy (relative)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid.

## Viva points
- Always dilute — the 1% lotion causes blistering
- Suitable for limited vitiligo and children
- Never treat on consecutive days

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.23 (PUVA — topical psoralen); Khopkar (Psoralens, PUVA and phototherapy). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
